Let me analyze this conflict.

Axis: num
- Register: "R117/2007-NL1-2015.02"
- Document: "R117-1/2007-NL1-15.02"

Looking at the certificate document text:
- The certificate number printed is "R117-1/2007-NL1-15.02"
- The comment says `num: R117/2007-NL1-2015.02`

The register value appears to be derived from the filename/URL: r117-2007-nl1-2015-02.pdf → R117/2007-NL1-2015.02.

The document's printed number is R117-1/2007-NL1-15.02 — note the "-1" after R117, likely indicating certificate series (R117-1 refers to the first part of the R117 recommendation, e.g., R117-1 for measuring systems, since OIML R117 is split into parts, and NMi issues "R117-1/2007-..." style numbers). Actually, the "R117-1/2007" is the OIML recommendation part designation (R117-1: Measuring systems for liquefied gases? Actually R117-1 might not be a formal part; NMi used the pattern "R117-1/2007-NL1-15.02" where -1 may be the certificate revision or part number). Regardless, this is the legally printed certificate number on the document.

Are these the same certificate? Both denote certificate 2015.02 (or 15.02) issued in 2015 by NL1 under R117/2007. The year format differs: "2015.02" vs "15.02" — year abbreviation difference. Also "R117/2007" vs "R117-1/2007" — the document includes "-1" which could denote part of the certificate or a revision. The filename uses 2015-02, and register normalized it to 2015.02.

So this is a number/year format difference that clearly denotes the same certificate → same-entity with the register's canonical form.

But wait — should the best value be the document's since the certificate is the legal instrument? The rule says: "Number/year format differences that clearly denote the same certificate = same-entity with the register's canonical form." So best_value = register's form: "R117/2007-NL1-2015.02".

Verdict: same-entity, best_value "R117/2007-NL1-2015.02".

Why: Both strings identify the same 2015 NL1 R117/2007 certificate; the document's "R117-1...15.02" is a formatting variant (part suffix and abbreviated year), so the register's canonical form wins per the format-drift rule.
